item.text: {"text":"[SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781) forms contextual states by attending to earlier interactions. Consequently, two positions can encode the same historical event: causal masking prevents future access but does not make their evidence independent. [BSARec](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28747) documents oversmoothing in sequential recommendation, where self-attention makes hidden representations similar. Together, these findings suggest that two high contextual-state similarities should not automatically count as two distinct supporting interactions.\n\nFor scores sorted s₁ ≥ s₂ ≥ …, top-two mean pooling, (s₁+s₂)/2, rewards multiple matches but allows an exceptionally large s₁ to compensate for weak s₂. Using s₂ directly expresses “at least two states exceed a threshold”: s₂ ≥ τ exactly when two or more scores reach τ. This is a mathematical property, not an established recommendation improvement, and correlated states still permit duplicated evidence. A hypothesis worth testing is to score individual historical item embeddings, or aggregate within separate history groups before taking the second-highest group score. [CARCA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.06519) provides precedent for candidate-conditioned aggregation across historical items, but does not establish independent corroboration. Compare max, top-two mean, and second-highest pooling under the same validation protocol; mask padding and define a fallback for histories shorter than two."}
